a.title: Measured wrapping priority
a.mechanism: Wrap by available content width using stable trigger nodes; adapt spacing and placement without replacing focused controls, open-panel launchers or their state. Keep trigger nodes and state stable across width changes.
a.visible: Title/completion, exact period, inclusion scope, counts and meaningful deadline exceptions.
a.disclosed: Details retains every metadata action; header and section summaries expose estimates and breakdown; diagnostics, inclusion and original menus remain reachable.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, stable DOM focus relationships, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure and 320px wrapping with reduced motion.
a.benefit: Responsive layout follows content pressure without trimming essential context.
a.risk: Threshold changes can cause distracting layout shifts.
a.verification: Resize with open menus and keyboard focus; test 320px/375px, long labels, reduced motion and selector preservation.

b.title: Steady metadata rail
b.mechanism: Keep one stable summary rail below each title; use a simple Details label for sparse metadata and remeasure expansion. Re-measure virtualized rows when local details expand. Skip empty rails and retain row measurements.
b.visible: Title, completion, exact period, active scope and wrapping summary.
b.disclosed: Rail opens all metadata with direct duration/price/date/frequency editing and time-of-day cycling; section/page rails expose breakdowns and scope controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Stable control positions support fast scanning as data changes.
b.risk: Reserved rail space can waste room on sparse tasks.
b.verification: Verify empty metadata, changing completion/counts, subtask totals, menus and virtualized row sizing.

a.title: Stable essential spine
a.mechanism: Retain the stable essential spine and inline definition lists; use object-specific accessible names, persistent selected period and inclusion state, separate completion targets, and existing Options menus with no hidden keyboard destinations. Keep completion separate and give every disclosure an object-specific name. Use object-specific accessible names and local definition lists.
a.visible: Essential spine and nonredundant date exceptions; inclusion state always stated. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Details expands semantic definition lists containing every datum and original action; header/section summaries use the same disclosure pattern, with diagnostic and inclusion controls retained. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Predictable focus structure keeps minimalism operable.
a.risk: Many Details buttons need object-specific accessible names.
a.verification: Verify tab order, expanded state, focus ring, all commands and no invisible focus targets.

b.title: One calm context tray
b.mechanism: Retain the calm context tray; show selected period and current inclusion scope in the closed tray, separate navigator and inclusion groups inside, and keep original summaries, diagnostics, menus and task editors reachable. Each scope and date control retains its independent callback and state. Separate period and scope groups and retain independent callbacks.
b.visible: Title, selected period, scope label, completion and essential deadline. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Tray expands existing period navigator, accumulated switch, duration breakdown and diagnostic; list and section options retain named routes; task panel contains all metadata editors. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: 44px buttons, semantic expansion, restored focus; keyboard access and opaque glass fallback. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: A single stable place carries supporting information.
b.risk: Combining scope and date could imply they share state.
b.verification: Check independent scope/date callbacks, duration, menus, completion and 320/375px.

a.title: Semantic one-line status replacement
a.mechanism: Replace duplicated progress indicators with one count-first status sentence that distinguishes own completion from included pending work using unchanged status calculations. Name both scopes explicitly using existing counts.
a.visible: Exact selected period, active inclusion scope, meaningful count sentence, task completion and relevant deadlines.
a.disclosed: The semantic status control opens the existing diagnostic; secondary disclosure preserves duration, inclusion and all task metadata; original menus stay separately scoped.
a.access: 44px status button, complete accessible name, wrapping count text, stable focus and keyboard access without duplicate spoken progress.
a.benefit: Removes redundant progress signals while keeping spoken information complete.
a.risk: A sentence may wrap differently as counts change.
a.verification: Test all_done, own-done/accumulated-pending, zero-goal and historical states; confirm diagnostic selectors and duration routes survive.

b.title: Completion lane
b.mechanism: Keep leading completion and trailing inspection lanes within bounded row width; use object-specific inspection labels and preserve current period, inclusion and original Start eligibility.
b.visible: Completion, titles, exact period, active scope and original Start action.
b.disclosed: Task Details preserves metadata; scoped Inspection retains estimates, diagnostics and inclusion; separate Options retains unchanged menus.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping completion/inspection targets, descriptive names, stable keyboard order, narrow-row wrapping and stopped event propagation.
b.benefit: Reduces accidental editing while marking many household tasks complete.
b.risk: Trailing controls may be distant on wide screens.
b.verification: Test partial repetitions, blocked tasks, accidental propagation, scope toggles and narrow lanes.

a.title: Resume-work compact header
a.mechanism: Keep the resume-work header and pending counts; use existing Start eligibility, show a concise disabled reason, keep historical period and inclusion scope visible, and retain named Summary, section Options and task Details. Start remains governed by existing eligible pending tasks. Keep existing disabled state and exact selected period.
a.visible: Empezar, list identity, period and pending tasks. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
a.disclosed: Resumen exposes full scope, diagnostic and estimates; section options and task details retain all properties, links and configuration. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
a.access: 44px Start, summary and detail controls; explicit disabled state when no pending reminders; visible focus. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
a.benefit: Makes resumption immediate without requiring a scan of every metric.
a.risk: Starting must retain existing eligibility and section scope.
a.verification: Verify disabled Start, section versus page start, historical periods, mixed routines and metadata editing without changing sequence semantics.

b.title: Native details groups
b.mechanism: Use native Details groups with scope-specific names outside clickable collapse regions; remeasure expanded rows and preserve independent section collapse and unchanged action callbacks. Place native Details outside clickable collapse regions.
b.visible: Titles, exact period, active scope, completion and named disclosure summaries.
b.disclosed: Opened groups retain inclusion, duration, diagnostics and every metadata editor/link; existing menus retain their original subjects and callbacks.
b.access: 44px native summaries, isolated events, visible keyboard focus, resilient text reflow and measured virtualized heights at zoom and 320px.
b.benefit: Uses predictable browser disclosure behavior with resilient text reflow.
b.risk: Virtualized list measurement must account for open details.
b.verification: Open nested groups at zoom, verify focus and heights, and test section collapse independently of metadata disclosure.

a.title: Context-first mobile folio
a.mechanism: Place a wrapping global context line before the task list in one column; repeat local captions only for real differences and retain meaningful deadlines next to their tasks. Repeat only true local differences.
a.visible: Exact period, inclusion scope, title/completion, counts and due exceptions.
a.disclosed: Full-width Details retains metadata actions and breakdowns; separate Options and inclusion controls preserve original commands and diagnostic routes.
a.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, explicit local names, readable long Spanish captions, keyboard disclosure and focus return at 320px.
a.benefit: Readable context establishes meaning before dense titles.
a.risk: More lines may delay the first task on initial load.
a.verification: Test long list/section/task titles, historical dates, rollover and scrolling without stale captions.

b.title: Persistent scope watermark
b.mechanism: Keep the persistent scope watermark as readable text and a 44px labelled scope button, show exact period nearby, and repeat only differing section scopes; its disclosure retains existing inclusion, estimate and diagnostic actions. Treat scope as explicit readable state, never a decorative watermark alone. Use visible labelled change control with readable state.
b.visible: Selected month, explicit own/combined scope text, titles and completion. Exact reference period and current inclusion scope remain readable.
b.disclosed: Watermark opens scope toggle with current state plus duration and diagnostic; task Details opens original metadata; list/section Options remains visible. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics. Retain every existing editor, action, link, diagnostic and scoped menu without duplicating command menus.
b.access: 44px watermark button, text rather than color signal, semantic state and keyboard access. Minimum 44px targets; visible keyboard focus; no hover-only routes; wrap at 320/375px; scoped reduced motion.
b.benefit: Scope survives even when supporting controls are disclosed.
b.risk: Too many differing scopes can repeat context.
b.verification: Verify section/global independence, own-done/accumulated-pending state, menus, dates and small widths.

a.title: Inherited context line
a.mechanism: Print labeled shared context once per matching block; show all differing deadlines, recurrence and scope, and describe inherited context without changing task settings. Only omit proven identical context; preserve uncertain values.
a.visible: Exact period, inclusion scope, titles/counts, completion and every meaningful context exception.
a.disclosed: Context exposes existing period navigation, inclusion and duration; task Details retains full original metadata and editors; Options preserves existing menus.
a.access: 44px contextual buttons, semantic exception text, explicit inherited-context descriptions, visible keyboard focus and wrapping at 320px.
a.benefit: Removes repeated information while making the source legible.
a.risk: Inherited context could be mistaken for a task's own setting.
a.verification: Verify differing frequencies, historical dates, same-period tasks, metadata editors and narrow wrapping.

b.title: Exception-led metadata with stable details
b.mechanism: Suppress only safely redundant metadata; always show overdue/divergent dates and keep labeled Details stable at each scope. Unknown or divergent context remains visible; Details is always explicit. Retain dates when context cannot be proven identical.
b.visible: Completion, title, exceptional dates, exact selected period and active scope/filter context.
b.disclosed: All nonexception metadata remains in Detalles; page/section options and summary preserve every statistic and edit action.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping targets, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure, visible focus/return, 320px wrapping and reduced motion.
b.benefit: Reduces repeated signals while keeping unusual obligations visible.
b.risk: A mistaken context comparison could suppress a needed date.
b.verification: Test mixed dates, overdue tasks, inherited frequencies and history; verify details always reveals complete values.
